title: Atomic Force Microscopy Imaging and Force Spectroscopy of Supported Lipid Bilayers
protocol: Prepare PBS buffer with concentrations of 2.7 mM KCl, 1.5 mM KH2PO4, 8 mM Na2HPO4, and 137 mM NaCl, pH 7.2.
Prepare SLB buffer at concentrations of 150 mM NaCl, 10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4.
Prepare a solution of 1 M CaCl2.
Dissolve di-oleoyl-phosphatidylcholine (DOPC) in chloroform at 25 mg/ml.
Dissolve sphingomyelin (SM) in chloroform at 25 mg/ml.
Dissolve cholesterol (Chol) in chloroform at 10 mg/ml.
Take 18.38 μl of DOPC, 17.10 μl of SM, and 11.30 μl of Chol to make a solution with 1 mg of total lipids in a 2:2:1 DOPC:SM:Chol molar ratio.
Mix the lipid solution completely by vortexing.
Add a fluorescent lipidic dye at 0.05 mol % if visualization is desired.
Dry off chloroform using N2 gas.
Further dry the lipid mixture under vacuum for at least 1 hr.
Displace air in excess lipids-in-chloroform vials with inert gas (N2, Ar or He).
Store lipid mixture and aliquots at -20 °C.
Dissolve dried lipids in PBS buffer to a concentration of 10 mg/ml.
Vortex the mixture vigorously for about 20 sec to 1 min.
Distribute cloudy suspension into 10 µl aliquots (1 mg of lipid makes 10 aliquots).
Store lipid aliquots at -20 °C until further use.
Take 10 µl of multilamellar lipid suspensions.
Add 150 µl of SLB buffer to the suspension.
Transfer the mixture into small (2 ml) capped glass vials.
Seal the vials with Parafilm.
Sonicate the mixture at room temperature in a bath sonicator for 10 min or until it becomes clear.
Take 10 µl of multilamellar lipid suspensions.
Add 150 µl of SLB buffer to the suspension.
Transfer the suspension into a cryogenic tube.
Freeze the lipid suspension by submerging the cryogenic tube in liquid nitrogen for a few seconds.
Thaw the lipid suspension by submerging the cryogenic tube in a water bath at room temperature or 37 °C for a few minutes.
Repeat the freeze-thaw steps at least 10 times.
Use a polycarbonate membrane with a 200 nm pore size and a commercial extrusion device to extrude the lipid suspension.
Equilibrate the extruder in water by passing water through the extruder.
Immerse the membrane in water.
Place the membrane between the two pistons, assemble the device and equilibrate in buffer, by passing the buffer through the extruder from one syringe to the other.
Take the lipid suspension using one syringe of the extruder ('dirty side').
Attach the syringe containing the lipid suspension on one chamber and the empty syringe on the opposing chamber.
Push the syringe on one end.
Pass the solution through the membrane and into the opposing syringe.
Repeat passing the solution through the membrane for a total of 31 times.
Check the membrane after extruding; if it was broken, repeat the extrusion process.
Empty the syringe into a small tube.
Wash coverslips first in water and then in ethanol.
Air dry the coverslips.
Peel off the outer layer of mica discs using adhesive tape.
Attach the mica disc onto the coverslip.
Attach plastic cylinders (2.5 cm outer diameter, 2 cm inner diameter, and 0.5 cm height) using optical glue/grease.
Pipette the whole liposome solution directly onto the mica.
Add more SLB buffer to reach a volume of 300 µl.
Add 0.9 µl of 1 M calcium chloride solution to reach a final concentration of 3 mM Ca2+.
Incubate at 37 °C for 2 min.
Cover the bilayers with buffer during incubation.
Incubate at 65 °C for at least 10 min.
Add more buffer as necessary, especially if incubating at higher temperatures.
Wash the bilayer with hot (65 °C) SLB buffer 15-20 times to remove calcium and unfused vesicles.
Keep the bilayer under buffer during washing steps.
Pipette the washing solution gently to avoid destroying the bilayer.
Cool supported bilayers to room temperature before AFM measurements.
Select a soft cantilever with a spring constant below 0.2 N/m.
Mount the selected cantilever to the AFM.
Turn on all vibration-isolation modules of the AFM system.
Wait for at least 15 minutes for equilibration and thermal drift reduction.
Approach the sample with the AFM tip until contact is made.
Use a Z-range of 1.5 µm for imaging lipid bilayers.
Select an initial region to image, such as 50 µm x 50 µm or 25 µm x 25 µm.
Adjust the set point during imaging to minimize force on the sample and correct thermal drift.
In contact mode, minimize the set point.
In tapping mode, maximize the set point.
Process images by fitting each scan line to polynomial leveling functions.
Perform line removal for scans that lose contact with the membrane using proprietary software.
Calibrate the cantilever following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Calibrate the tip’s sensitivity to measure deflection as z-piezo movement instead of electrical signal in volts.
Calculate the cantilever spring constant using the thermal noise frequency method.
Plot the amplitude of vibration from noise with respect to frequency of oscillation.
Fit a Lorentzian function around the peak to automatically calculate the spring constant.
Select a 5 µm x 5 µm region in the bilayer for force spectroscopy.
Set up the AFM to take force curves in a 16 x 16 grid within the selected region.
Ensure a 100 nm distance between two neighboring points to avoid overlapping membrane areas.
Divide the 5 µm x 5 µm region into a 16 x 16 grid for precise measurements.
Set z-piezo displacement to 400 nm to ensure full retraction of the cantilever between measurements.
Set approach speed to 800 nm/sec.
Set retract speed to 200 nm/sec.
Acquire force curves by pressing the “run” button in the AFM software.
Save force curves as force vs. height curves.
Correct for cantilever bending using the AFM software during data processing.
Calculate tip-sample separation by subtracting vertical deflection from piezo movement.
Identify breakthrough force of the membrane from the approach force curve peak.
Determine thickness of the membrane from the difference between breakthrough force position and rising force point position.
Acquire at least 500 force curves for each condition to obtain good statistics.
Plot a histogram of the values using programs like Origin or MatLab.
Fit histograms to a Gaussian distribution to get the peak and width of the distribution.
